messages.content: my brother and i tried to cook together yesterday. we both started doing the same part and left another part until too late. i want to try again without making it all about who was wrong.
you could talk about the order of the work rather than which person did something wrong. what needed to happen first, and which part did both of you start?
we both washed the vegetables. nobody started the rice. then the vegetables were ready before the rice was cooked.
then you can say you did not choose clearly who would do each part. next time, one person can wash the vegetables while the other starts the rice. after that, you can check what needs doing next.
he likes cooking the vegetables. i do not mind doing the rice.
that gives you a simple start. you can make the rice while he gets the vegetables ready. you can still help each other after your first part is done.
write a message asking if that plan works for him.
would you like to cook together again? i could start the rice while you get the vegetables ready. then we can check what is left to do. would that work for you?
he said yes, but he needs me to wash the vegetables before he comes home.
then the new order starts before he gets home. you wash the vegetables first. when it is time to cook, you start the rice and he cooks the vegetables.
make that one sentence.
i will wash the vegetables before you get home, then start the rice while you cook the vegetables.
i want to ask my grandfather about the work he did when he was young. i only know he worked in a shop. i do not know how to start.
you could begin with a question about a day there. that gives him a place to start without asking him to tell his whole life at once.
what would that question be?
what was a day at the shop like when you first worked there?
how can i keep the question simple?
you could ask about one day at work. he can tell you what he did when he came in and what happened after that.
he said he opened the shop before the other worker came. i want to hear more about that part.
you could ask what he had to get ready before the other worker came. did he put things on the shelf, clean the room, or do something else?
should i give all those choices in my question?
you do not have to. a short question can leave room for his own answer: what did you do after opening the shop?
he says he liked the quiet before people came in. i like a quiet morning too.
then you have something to share as well as another question. you could say: i like a quiet morning too. did the shop get busy soon after opening?
i want it to be a conversation, not only question after question.
saying that you like a quiet morning gives him something about you to answer. you can listen to what he says next rather than choosing another question before he has finished.
i moved a plant from near the window to the middle of the room. now it looks different. can i say the move made it change?
you know the change happened after you moved it. that gives you something to look at, but it does not tell you by itself that the move was the only reason. what looks different?
the leaves look less green. i am not asking you to know the right care from that alone.
then we can keep what you saw clear: the leaves look less green than before, and this happened after you moved the plant. you have not yet said whether anything else changed.
i also gave it more water last week. i forgot about that.
then there are two changes to keep in mind: the place and the water. write down what you remember before choosing just one as the reason.
i do not need a long list. make a short note for me.
i moved the plant away from the window and gave it more water last week. now the leaves look less green. i do not yet know why.
why keep i do not know why at the end?
it makes clear what you saw and what you still do not know. your note can be useful without saying the reason is known.
what could i ask someone who knows more about this type of plant?
i moved this plant and changed how much water i gave it. the leaves now look less green. what information would help you understand what is happening?
i have a photo of my family sitting around a table. i want a short sentence for it, but i do not want to say everyone was happy because i do not know that.
you can write about the moment without choosing a feeling for everyone. for example: a meal together around the table.
we were not eating yet. we were waiting for my uncle to bring the food.
then you could write: together at the table, waiting for the meal. that keeps the part you know and does not say the food was already there.
i want to say my grandmother was telling a story, because she was.
then add that detail: waiting for the meal while my grandmother told us a story.
can it sound more like something i would say to a friend?
we were waiting for the food, and my grandmother started telling us a story.
she had already started before the photo was taken. i do not know when she began.
then keep started out of the sentence: we were waiting for the food while my grandmother told us a story.
what does while add?
it puts the waiting and the story together in time. it does not say the story began at the same moment as the waiting.
make it shorter but keep both parts.
waiting for food and listening to my grandmother tell a story.
i have to read to other people at school. i can read quietly, but when people listen i lose my place.
you could try reading a short part to one person first. if you lose your place, stop and find the line again. you do not have to start the whole page over each time.
i have been trying with my sister. she waits for me, but i feel like i should read as fast as she does.
you can work on being clear before being fast. your sister has her own way of reading. the useful question is whether you can follow the words and be understood.
what can i ask her to do while i read?
you could ask her to listen until you finish one part, then tell you if there was a sentence she could not understand. that keeps the help specific.
i do not want her to stop me after every word.
then say that before you begin: please let me finish this part first. after that, we can go back to any word i need help with.
what if i do not know where i am on the page?
you can stop and say you need to find your place. take a moment, look for the line, and begin again from a part you know. that does not make the rest of your reading wrong.
write a short thing i can say to the teacher.
i sometimes lose my place when i read to other people. could i have a moment to find the line if that happens?
i have a tool from my friend. i said i would bring it back today, but now they say they will not be home until late. should i leave it by their door?
you can ask where they would like you to put it. the tool is theirs, and a place by the door may not be where they want it left.
i do not want to ask a long question. just make it clear.
where would you like me to leave the tool if you are not home?
they say i can bring it tomorrow instead. does that change what i said about today?
yes. you first said you would bring it today, and now your friend has said tomorrow is okay. you can answer so both of you know that is the new plan.
write the answer.
thank you. i will keep it here today and bring it back tomorrow.
i have not said i can go tomorrow morning. do not choose a time.
that answer leaves the time open. it says tomorrow without saying morning or afternoon.
now ask what time works for them.
what time tomorrow would be good for me to bring it back?
they say after dinner, but i work then. i can go before lunch.
you could say: i work after dinner, but i can come before lunch. would that work, or should we choose another day?
in a story, some children went outside and some stayed in the room. my son says that must mean all the children went outside. how can i explain the difference?
you can point to the two groups in the sentence. one group went outside, and another stayed inside. all would put every child in the same group, but this sentence does not.
can i use five children as an example?
yes. you could say three children went outside and two stayed in the room. then all five are part of the story, but only three went outside.
what if i just say some children went outside and nothing else?
then you know one or more children went outside. the sentence alone does not tell you whether the other children did too. you need more information before saying how many stayed inside.
i thought some always had the meaning not all.
people often use it that way in conversation, but the word alone does not always give that whole meaning. adding some stayed inside makes the other group clear.
keep that explanation very simple for my son.
if i only say some went outside, ask about the other children. if i also say some stayed inside, you know not everyone went outside.
can you ask him a question with the five children example?
three children went outside and two stayed inside. how many children went outside?
he says five.
five is how many children there are together. the number who went outside is three. the other two stayed in the room.
picoboi, i asked whether my brother put the book on the table. now tell me where the book is.
you have asked about the table, but you have not given an answer. i do not know where the book is from the question alone.
why not use the table as the answer?
because asking whether something happened does not say it happened. the table is one possible place in your question, rather than a known place for the book.
my brother says he put it on the shelf. now what do you know?
your brother says he put the book on the shelf. that is the new information you gave me.
can you say i have seen it there?
no. you told me what your brother said. you have not said you saw the book yourself.
now i went to the shelf and found it. make a short sentence about that.
i found the book on the shelf.
why did you use i there?
you asked for a sentence about what you did. i wrote it as something you could say yourself. if i say it to you about you, i would say you found the book on the shelf.
okay, give me that sentence using you, and add that my brother was right about the place.
you found the book on the shelf, where your brother said he had put it.
